pr_title: Fix import and saving related crashes
pr_body:
* Don't add empty mesh to result when importing obj files
* Check for null resources in `ResourceSaver`

This adds the check from `core_bind` to `ResourceSaver` directly, ~could remove the one in `ResourceSaver.save` in `core_bind` as it's now redundant, but just added it for now~, it helps catch broken cases when doing things from c++

The obj side avoids doing any of the remaining code, makes things a bit clearer, and matches the code here:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/fe01776f05b1787b28b4a270d53037a3c25f4ca2/editor/import/3d/resource_importer_obj.cpp#L441-L445

For this specific case we might want to look at adding support for lines in obj files as they support it, or a more clear error message or warning when using unsupported features, but that's outside the scope of this

---

* Fixes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/89776

I would remove the redundant `core_bind` checks then, as it seems to be wasteful for performance to do these checks twice.

issue_context.title: Importing a line only obj crash Godot Editor
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproductible in 4.3-dev5

### System information

Windows 10 - Godot 4.3-dev5 Vulkan (Forward+)

### Issue description

When importing a simple obj with only lines inside, Godot crashes.

### Steps to reproduce

Just import the provided file in a Godot project

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Create a new project and copy the provided obj file into it.
[profil.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/14720714/profil.zip)
comments: Seems like the importer doesn't handle lines which probably causes the data to be invalid, will look at a fix
Found the issue and writing a fix, will open a PR soon

Nice. Thanks for the quick fix. I hope this report helped to make Godot more robust. As I understand the comit, loading the resource will result in a null mesh right ? I will not be able to get the vertex positions and lines (obvously for the lines as the Mesh doesn't seems to have lines) ?

Note it not necessarily a problem, it's just to know :)
As per my comment there it'd be a future change to add support for lines, this just fixes the crash, the mesh won't be imported at all
